The part of Business Intelligence I care about most is the part nobody sees:
knowing where a number comes from before it reaches a dashboard someone uses to
make a decision.

I learned that over 676 hours in the BI team at PKF Attest, the only intern in a
team of eight, working across three live client accounts. On one of them the
figures would not reconcile: data was arriving from two systems that had never
been centralised, so records were counted twice and every calculation on top of
them was wrong. Finding that is not glamorous, but it is the difference between a
report people trust and one they quietly stop opening.

The other half of the job is being understood. Clients often ask for a chart
their data cannot support, so I study the dataset first and then walk them
through what is actually there. I trained as a teacher alongside my Mathematics
degree, which is where that habit comes from, and the Mathematics is why I am
comfortable being asked whether a result is significant, not just whether the
chart looks right. I work mainly in Power BI and SQL, with Python and R for
analysis.

This site is one of my two Bachelor's theses: an exploratory analysis in R of
what drives downloads of educational math apps. The short answer is that only
reward systems are linked to more downloads, and popularity is not a proxy for
quality, a finding that survives a full robustness protocol.

I am looking for a junior Data Analyst or BI role in an international,
English-speaking data team, with technical depth and room to grow. I am open across Europe. As an EU citizen, I do not need a
work permit.

**Languages:** Spanish (native), English (C1), French (basic).
